recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If future builds again report false unused-binding hints, investigate HL7/kindling's ResourceValidator rather than this core spec source checkout; no current follow-up was found.
issue_request: FHIR-5615 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and asked that generator warnings about bindings not being used stop ignoring profile-defined or profile-used bindings. The decisive Jira comment says to remove the hint because it was more trouble than it was worth, citing SVN revision 4549.
initial_application: Git commit c65988b6eb544d9a09ca0313baed37ffc9d7a5f0, imported from SVN revision 4549, deleted the ResourceValidator hint that emitted "Binding is not used" when a binding's element type was unknown.
additional_context: Commit 9f549566d1346cad7db6d2afca6080d7cebdfbbe later removed the old in-repo tools/java validator source when the build switched to a Gradle dependency on HL7/kindling. The active build.gradle.kts depends on org.hl7.fhir:kindling and runs org.hl7.fhir.tools.publisher.Publisher. A pinned check of HL7/kindling at 8655559ffed4ce52874fdfaf2e247d0b5b0b0260 found no "Binding is not used" text in ResourceValidator, and community searches found no later reversal.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The exact obsolete warning text is absent from the current checkout, the historical local validator source is no longer build scope, and the current external Kindling validator used by the build does not reintroduce the warning.
